column1: radical§The radical of the word survives in six languages.§这个词的**词根**在六种语言中留存下来。
raid§The raid on the archive was carried out with trolleys.§这次对档案室的“**突袭**”是用推车完成的。
raiment§Fine raiment in the inventory means the household had money.§清单上**华美的衣物**说明这户人家有钱。
ramble§A Sunday ramble covers eight miles and three counties.§周日的一次**漫步**走过八英里、三个郡。
rambunctious§A rambunctious puppy is a poor companion for an archive.§**活蹦乱跳**的小狗不适合陪着整理档案。
ramshackle§The argument is ramshackle and somehow holds together.§这个论证**摇摇欲坠**，却不知怎么撑住了。
rancor§There is no rancor in the letter, only exhaustion.§这封信里没有**怨恨**，只有疲惫。
rancorous§A rancorous footnote outlived both the men it concerned.§一条**怀恨**的脚注比它涉及的两个人活得都久。
rapport§Rapport cannot be scheduled and is obvious when it happens.§**融洽**无法安排，一旦发生却显而易见。
rapturous§A rapturous first reading is worth distrusting.§第一次读得**心醉神迷**，值得怀疑。
rashly§Do not rashly delete anything you cannot recreate.§不要**草率**删掉任何你无法重建的东西。
ratify§The treaty was signed in March and ratified in December.§条约三月签署，十二月**批准**。
rational§There is a rational explanation and it is duller than the rumor.§有一个**理性**的解释，比谣言乏味得多。
rationalism§Rationalism and empiricism are less opposed than the textbooks say.§**理性主义**与经验主义的对立，没有教科书说的那么大。
rationality§Bounded rationality explains more decisions than pure logic.§**有限理性**比纯粹逻辑更能解释多数决策。
rationalization§Every rationalization begins with a real feeling.§每一次**合理化**都始于一种真实的感受。
rationalize§They rationalized four warehouses into one and lost the stock records.§他们把四个仓库**合并成一个**，却丢了库存记录。
raze§Fire razed the quarter and the street plan survived.§大火**夷平**了这个街区，街道格局却留了下来。
reactionary§Calling a caution reactionary ends the conversation cheaply.§把谨慎说成**反动**，是一种廉价的终结谈话的方式。
reactive§A reactive department is always a year behind.§**被动应对**的部门永远落后一年。
reaffirm§He reaffirmed the finding and revised the explanation.§他**重申**了这个发现，修改了解释。
realign§Realigning the road cost more than replacing the bridge.§**道路改线**比换桥还贵。
realistic§Be realistic about the schedule and ambitious about the question.§在进度上**现实**，在问题上有野心。
realization§The realization that nobody was coming took ten minutes.§过了十分钟才**意识到**没人会来。
reap§You reap the sample you sowed, however you analyse it.§不管怎么分析，你**收获**的都是你抽取的那个样本。
reappraise§An artist worth reappraising is usually one who was famous once.§值得**重新评价**的艺术家，通常曾经出名过。
rearrange§Rearranging the furniture changed how the seminar went.§**重新摆放**家具改变了研讨课的进行方式。
reassure§Do not reassure people with a figure you have not checked.§不要用一个自己没核对过的数字去**安抚**别人。
rebate§The rebate applies only if you claim it within a month.§这项**返款**只有在一个月内申请才有效。
rebel§He rebelled against a method he later taught for thirty years.§他**反抗**过的方法，后来自己教了三十年。
rebellion§A rebellion in the ranks is usually about the rota.§队伍里的“**造反**”通常是为了排班表。
rebellious§A rebellious edition restored the passages the censor cut.§一个**叛逆**的版本恢复了审查者删去的段落。
recalcitrance§Recalcitrance in a machine is usually dirt.§机器的“**闹别扭**”通常是脏了。
recalcitrant§A recalcitrant witness is not necessarily a lying one.§**不肯配合**的证人未必在撒谎。
recant§Under pressure he recanted and under more pressure he did not.§在压力下他**放弃**了主张，在更大的压力下却没有。
receptivity§Receptivity falls sharply after ninety minutes.§九十分钟后，**接受能力**急剧下降。
recessive§A recessive gene surfaces once in four generations here.§这里的**隐性**基因每四代显现一次。
reciprocate§She reciprocated with a letter twice as long.§她回了一封长一倍的信作为**回报**。
reclaim§He reclaimed an hour a day by not reading the news.§他靠不看新闻，每天**夺回**一小时。
reclusive§A reclusive habit is not the same as a hostile one.§**隐居的**习惯与敌意不是一回事。
recognition§Recognition of the handwriting settled the attribution.§对笔迹的**辨认**解决了归属问题。
recollect§I recollect the room clearly and the year not at all.§我清楚地**记得**那个房间，年份却完全想不起。
recommence§After a pause of forty years the excavation recommenced.§中断四十年后，发掘**重新开始**。
recommendation§Take the recommendation and check the reasoning anyway.§接受这条**建议**，但仍要核对它的推理。
reconcile§The accounts finally reconciled to within a penny.§账目最终**对上了**，误差不到一便士。
reconciliation§Reconciliation of the two datasets took a whole term.§两组数据的**对账**花了整整一个学期。
reconstituted§Reconstituted from three fragments, the vase is mostly plaster.§这只瓶子由三块碎片**复原**，大部分是石膏。
recourse§Without recourse to the archive, the claim cannot be tested.§不**借助**档案，这个说法无法验证。
recrimination§Recrimination is what happens when nobody kept notes.§没人做记录时，剩下的就是**相互指责**。
recruit§New recruits are given the worst desk and the best mentor.§**新人**分到最差的桌子和最好的导师。
rectitude§Rectitude without judgment is just a longer route to the same harm.§没有判断力的**正直**，只是通往同样伤害的更长路径。
redeem§He redeemed the coupon four years after it expired.§他在优惠券过期四年后才**兑换**。
redemptive§There is nothing redemptive about suffering you could have avoided.§本可避免的痛苦并没有什么**救赎**意义。
rediscover§She rediscovered her own note and disagreed with it.§她**重新发现**了自己写的批注，并且不同意它。
redolent§The whole book is redolent of a decade it never names.§整本书都**弥漫着**一个它从未点名的年代的气息。
redouble§The rain redoubled and the search was called off.§雨势**加倍**，搜寻被取消。
redundancy§Redundancy in a safety system is a feature, not waste.§安全系统中的**冗余**是特性，不是浪费。
redundant§The second engine is redundant until the first one stops.§第二台发动机是**多余的**，直到第一台停下来。
refine§He refined the question until it could be answered.§他不断**打磨**这个问题，直到它可以被回答。
reflective§A reflective surface doubled the light in a dark room.§一个**反光面**让暗房间的光线翻倍。
refract§The prism refracts blue more sharply than red.§棱镜对蓝光的**折射**比红光更强。
refund§No refund was offered and none was asked for.§没有提供**退款**，也没有人要求。
refurbish§A refurbished machine is not the same as a new one.§**翻新**的机器与新机器不是一回事。
refutation§A refutation that nobody reads leaves the error standing.§没人读的**反驳**，只会让错误继续存在。
refute§You cannot refute a claim that was never precisely made.§你无法**驳倒**一个从未被精确表述的主张。
regal§The regal blue of the binding has not faded at all.§装帧上那种**帝王**般的蓝色一点也没褪。
regenerate§Skin regenerates completely in about a month.§皮肤大约一个月就完全**再生**一次。
